A simulation spec from an AlphaSimR script

Source: R/alphasim.R
alphasim_program.Rd

Turns an AlphaSimR breeding scheme into a tunable spec. You write one replicate of the scheme as a function of the founders, the SimParam and your design arguments; tidyagsim builds the founders for each replicate, seeds the random numbers, runs every design on the same seeds and collects the results. Mark any argument with tune() to search over it.

Usage

alphasim_program(
  program,
  ...,
  founders = asr_founders(),
  params = list(),
  check = NULL,
  metrics = NULL
)

Arguments

program

A function whose first two arguments are founders (an AlphaSimR Pop) and SP, followed by design arguments. It returns a named list of outcomes.

...

Values for program's arguments and for any asr_founders() field; use tune() to mark one for tuning.

founders

An asr_founders() recipe.

params

Named list of parameter objects (see sim_param()) giving ranges for tuned arguments.

check

Optional function of the design arguments returning NULL when a design is feasible or a reason string when it is not.

metrics

Optional default sim_metric_set().

Value

An alphasim_program spec.

Details

Inside program, SP is also bound globally while it runs, so AlphaSimR calls work with or without simParam = SP.

Use asr_tracker() inside program to record the population each year and asr_summary() to turn the record into the built-in breeding metrics (release_gain, gain_per_year, genetic_variance, cost, ...).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
recurrent <- alphasim_program(
  function(founders, SP, n_select, cycles) {
    tr <- asr_tracker(founders)
    pop <- founders
    for (cycle in seq_len(cycles)) {
      pop <- AlphaSimR::setPheno(pop)
      parents <- AlphaSimR::selectInd(pop, n_select)
      pop <- AlphaSimR::randCross(parents, nCrosses = 100)
      tr$record(pop, year = cycle, cost = 100 * 15)
    }
    asr_summary(tr)
  },
  n_select = tune(), cycles = 5,
  founders = asr_founders(n_chr = 5, seg_sites = 100),
  params = list(n_select = sim_param(c(5, 40)))
)
res <- tune_grid(recurrent, sim_replicates(10), grid = 5)
autoplot(res)
} # }
